titleEn: X Spaces: Free speech with Alex Jones
titleZh: X Spaces：与亚历克斯·琼斯谈言论自由
summaryEn: After reinstating Alex Jones's account, Musk joined a nearly three-hour X Space hosted by Mario Nawfal with Jones, Vivek Ramaswamy and Andrew Tate to debate free speech; it drew millions of live listeners.
summaryZh: 恢复亚历克斯·琼斯的账号后，马斯克参加了由马里奥·纳瓦尔主持、琼斯、维韦克·拉马斯瓦米和安德鲁·泰特参与的一场近3小时的 X Space，围绕言论自由展开辩论；直播吸引了数百万听众。

segments.textEn: My initial thoughts since we've got a pretty cool panel already up.
segments.textZh: 既然已经有了一个相当不错的嘉宾阵容，先说说我的初步想法。

segments.textEn: Laura, your initial thoughts about Alex being back on X?
segments.textZh: 劳拉，你对亚历克斯重返 X 的初步看法是什么？

segments.textEn: Well, I love it. I mean, I'm thrilled to see him back on X and it's really like personal for me personally, because a lot of people forget about this. But on September 5, 2018, Alex and I went to the congressional hearing on big tech censorship together and oh, he just texted me. He said he's locked out. So I wonder how he can do this.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我很喜欢。我的意思是，看到他重返 X，我非常激动，而且这对我个人而言确实很有切身意义，因为很多人都忘了这件事。但在2018年9月5日，亚历克斯和我一起去参加了关于大型科技公司审查制度的国会听证会，而且，哦，他刚刚给我发了短信。他说自己被锁在外面了。所以我不知道他怎么才能参与。

segments.textEn: Yeah, that's very weird. Make sure no one hasn't blocked. By the way, guys, that's Zev. Make sure you don't have. You weren't even on Twitter when.
segments.textZh: 是啊，这非常奇怪。确保没有人没有屏蔽。顺便说一下，各位，那是泽夫。确保你没有。那时候你甚至都不在 Twitter 上。

segments.textEn: That's interesting.
segments.textZh: 这很有意思。

segments.textEn: But we, we attended the congressional hearing on big tech censorship when Jack Dorsey was testifying. And I just want to remind everybody that this was back when. Okay, so he said. Sorry, he said, joining now. He said Chase Geyser is going to let him use his account. So you need to make Chase Geyser a speaker because that's the account Alex will be using since he said that he can't do a space from his account. So just make Chase Geyser Speaker Mario,
segments.textZh: 但我们，我们参加了杰克·多尔西作证时关于大型科技公司审查制度的国会听证会。而且我只想提醒大家，那是在当时。好的，所以他说。抱歉，他说，现在加入。他说蔡斯·盖泽会让他使用自己的账号。所以你需要把蔡斯·盖泽设为发言人，因为亚历克斯会使用那个账号，因为他说自己无法通过自己的账号开 Space。所以马里奥，把蔡斯·盖泽设为发言人，

segments.textEn: you know, watch him get banned for
segments.textZh: 你知道，等着看他因为

segments.textEn: like a account evasion or whatever.
segments.textZh: 类似规避账号封禁之类的原因被封禁吧。

segments.textEn: Yeah.
segments.textZh: 是啊。

segments.textEn: So you were saying, what were you saying, Tony? Laura, let me finish.
segments.textZh: 所以你刚才说，你刚才说什么，托尼？劳拉，让我说完。

segments.textEn: So what I was saying is that this was in 2018, in September. So mind you, Republicans still had control of the House and the Senate and Trump was in the White House and so you had a Republican controlled House Oversight Committee. And this, this actually was my pin tweet. And I'll, I'll send you, I'll put it in the, the nest so everyone can see it. But I called Jack Dorsey out. This is when I stood up and I said, you know, you're lying.
segments.textZh: 所以我刚才说的是，这件事发生在2018年9月。所以请注意，共和党当时仍然控制着众议院和参议院，特朗普在白宫，因此众议院监督委员会由共和党控制。而这，这其实是我的置顶推文。而且我会，我会发给你，我会把它放到，放到顶端，让所有人都能看到。但我当面质问了杰克·多尔西。那就是我站起来说，你知道，你在撒谎的时候。

segments.textEn: You're censoring conservatives. You censored me. You censored Alex Jones, James o' Keefe, and you're trying to steal the election. And I warned the Republicans of what was going to happen. Literally the very next day after that hearing, right? We, Alex and I chased Jack Dorsey out of Congress. It's literally on video. And there is this iconic photo. It's actually his Twitter banner photo right now. And you can see Alex like screaming at Jack Dorsey and then you see me with my pink selfie stick.
segments.textZh: 你们在审查保守派。你们审查了我。你们审查了亚历克斯·琼斯、詹姆斯·奥基夫，而且你们还试图窃取选举。我警告过共和党人将会发生什么。就在那场听证会之后的第二天，对吧？我们，亚历克斯和我，把杰克·多西一路追出了国会。这确实有视频为证。还有一张标志性的照片。实际上，那现在就是他的 Twitter 横幅照片。你可以看到亚历克斯像是在对杰克·多西大喊，然后你会看到我拿着粉色自拍杆。

segments.textEn: The very next day, Alex was permanently banned from Twitter and so was the Infowars account. And so just the fact that, you know, we have been dealing with this level of persecution together for so many years. You know, we were really? The canaries in the coal mine. And Alex has had me on his show many times and has said that I'm the most censored woman in America. He's probably the most censored.
segments.textZh: 就在第二天，亚历克斯被 Twitter 永久封禁，Infowars 账号也是如此。所以，光是这个事实，你知道，这么多年来我们一直共同面对这种程度的迫害。你知道，我们真的是？煤矿里的金丝雀。亚历克斯曾多次邀请我上他的节目，还说我是美国受审查最严重的女性。他可能是受审查最严重的。

segments.textEn: So we've got the most censored men and women on stage. So it's a testament to what AX has achieved.
segments.textZh: 所以，台上聚集了受审查最严重的男性和女性。所以，这证明了 AX 所取得的成就。

segments.textEn: That's right.
segments.textZh: 没错。

segments.textEn: Yes, we can.
segments.textZh: 是的，我们可以。

segments.textEn: Alex, let's go.
segments.textZh: 亚历克斯，开始吧。

segments.textEn: It is.
segments.textZh: 确实如此。

segments.textEn: It is. Alex, welcome to X. How are you?
segments.textZh: 确实如此。亚历克斯，欢迎来到 X。你好吗？

segments.textEn: Thanks for having me. Just so I don't get in trouble or Chase Geiser doesn't get troublesome, I really try to follow all the rules so they can't try to get me off with all the complaints that the woke thought police engage in. Chase Deisner works here at Infowars. He's co hosting with me tonight on my regular show at Infowars. And so I've been very happy to come on. I know this is the biggest or one of the biggest spaces here on Twitter, so I'm very honored to be here.
segments.textZh: 谢谢你们邀请我。为了不让我惹上麻烦，也不让蔡斯·盖泽惹上麻烦，我确实努力遵守所有规则，这样他们就不能利用觉醒派思想警察提出的所有投诉来设法把我赶出去。蔡斯·戴斯纳在 Infowars 工作。今晚他在 Infowars 我的常规节目中和我共同主持。所以我一直非常高兴能来参加。我知道这是 Twitter 上规模最大或最大的 Space 之一，所以我很荣幸能来到这里。

segments.textEn: And then I've been frantically trying to get on, but I think the code hasn't propagated yet. I'm not an IT guy, but I think the code hasn't propagated because I'm still locked out of a lot of features and a lot of things. And I was unable to get verified today until Jack Bosobic called some folks he knew at Twitter and they were able to even allow me to get on the Twitter. So I'm here and as soon as they fix that glitch, I'll be glad to call in from my phone.
segments.textZh: 然后我一直在拼命尝试加入，但我认为代码还没有生效。我不是 IT 人员，但我认为代码还没有生效，因为我仍然无法使用很多功能和其他许多东西。而且我今天一直无法获得认证，直到杰克·博索比克给他在 Twitter 认识的一些人打了电话，他们才得以让我登录 Twitter。所以我现在在这里，等他们一修复那个故障，我就很乐意用手机打进来。

segments.textEn: But for now I'm with Chase Geyser.
segments.textZh: 但目前我和蔡斯·盖泽在一起。

segments.textEn: Yeah, we've just got. We just got Jack up on stage as well. He just came up now. So, Jack, we appreciate you trying to fix. So what happens, Alex, when you try to join the space from your account? You can't see the space, so it doesn't allow you to join.
segments.textZh: 是的，我们刚刚让。我们也刚刚让杰克上台了。他现在刚上来。所以，杰克，我们感谢你设法修复。那么，亚历克斯，当你尝试从自己的账号加入这个空间时，会发生什么？你看不到这个空间，所以它不允许你加入。

segments.textEn: Wow.
segments.textZh: 哇。

segments.textEn: Wow.
segments.textZh: 哇。
segments.speakerZh: 乔西（红发自由意志主义者）

segments.textEn: Did you hear me? Did you hear me, Alex? What happens? So when you try to join, does it just not show the space or you can't click and join?
segments.textZh: 你听见我说话了吗？你听见我了吗，亚历克斯？怎么回事？所以当你尝试加入时，是根本不显示这个空间，还是你无法点击加入？

segments.textEn: No, no, it lets me begin to join. And then it sent me an error message saying, your account is banned. I have a screenshot of it.
segments.textZh: 不，不，它让我开始加入。然后它给我发了一条错误消息，说：你的账户已被封禁。我有它的截图。

segments.textEn: Oh, wow. Okay. It could be just technical. Well, how. First question that I have for you, we've got a pretty. Pretty incredible panel. A lot of people that you probably know. We're going to go to the panel in a bit as well for questions. But, you know, first I want to applaud you for coming here. You could have gone anywhere, but you came on a platform that, you know, we ask the hard questions. We always try to represent all sides of every discussion and avoid echo chambers.
segments.textZh: 哦，哇。好的。可能只是技术问题。嗯，怎么说。我想问你的第一个问题，我们有一个相当。相当了不起的嘉宾阵容。很多人你可能都认识。过一会儿我们也会请嘉宾们提问。但是，你知道，首先我想为你来到这里而称赞你。你本可以去任何地方，但你来到了一个，你知道，我们会提出尖锐问题的平台。我们始终努力呈现每场讨论的各方观点，并避免回音室效应。

segments.textEn: And that was the first place you came on as you got reinstated on X. So I want to applaud that step.
segments.textZh: 而且在你的 X 账户恢复后，这里是你最先来的地方。所以我想为你迈出这一步而称赞你。

segments.textEn: First question I have for you, how
segments.textZh: 我想问你的第一个问题是，怎么

segments.textEn: does it feel to be back?
segments.textZh: 回来是什么感觉？

segments.textEn: Well, I've got to say, it's not about me. It's about everybody having the courage to stand up for free speech, particularly Elon Musk, Tucker Carlson and others.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我得说，这不是关于我。这关乎每个人都有勇气捍卫言论自由，尤其是埃隆·马斯克、塔克·卡尔森等人。

segments.textEn: Because when we put up with somebody else being censored for whatever reason the media says or whether something they said that was wrong or something that hurts our feelings, when we censor somebody else or go along with it, we end up censoring everybody else, including ourselves. So I want to applaud everybody for after five, six years of this nightmare, for waking up to the truth of what's really going on. And so it's very exciting.
segments.textZh: 因为当别人因媒体所说的任何理由，或是因为他们说了什么错误的话，或是说了什么伤害我们感情的话而遭到审查，而我们容忍这种事时；当我们审查别人或对此表示认同时，最终我们会审查其他所有人，包括我们自己。所以我想称赞每一个人，在经历这场长达5、6年的噩梦后，终于醒悟过来，看清了真正在发生的事情。所以这非常令人振奋。

segments.textEn: I feel like the tide has really turned. And I'm not just seeing this, you know, here in cyberspace on Twitter, which has obviously exploded and just is dominating while the old big tech dinosaurs die because they are like Pravda in the old Soviet Union. So it's very, very exciting to be part of history. But really this isn't about me. This is about the public recognizing that the process that was used to demonize me, misrepresent what I said and did, and then silence me and then build strawmen.
segments.textZh: 我觉得潮流确实已经逆转。而且我不只是在网络空间的 Twitter 上看到这一点，你知道，Twitter 显然已经爆发式增长，正占据主导地位，而那些老牌大型科技恐龙正在消亡，因为它们就像旧苏联的《真理报》。所以，能成为历史的一部分非常、非常令人振奋。但其实这不是关于我。这关乎公众认识到，他们用来妖魔化我、歪曲我的言行，然后让我噤声，再树立稻草人的那套过程。

segments.textEn: Once they silence you off all major platforms, they're able to then steal your identity and then turn you into something you weren't with edited clips and out of context stuff. And now even everybody's experiencing it is prominent with these deep fakes. So that's why it's so important that everybody have a voice, even if we disagree with them, because we need to hear what they actually have to say in real time. Especially in this so connected world.
segments.textZh: 一旦他们让你在所有主要平台上噤声，他们随后就能窃取你的身份，再通过剪辑过的片段和脱离语境的内容，把你变成一个你本来不是的人。而现在，随着这些深度伪造技术，就连每个人都正在明显经历这种事。所以，让每个人都有发声的机会才如此重要，即使我们不同意他们，因为我们需要实时听到他们实际上要说什么。尤其是在这个联系如此紧密的世界里。

segments.textEn: Because this is the real discrimination of the future with these social credit scores and AI systems is using excuses to block humans off the web, but then giving bots free reign. That's another visionary thing that Elon Musk has done is declare war on the bots, declare war on robots that are stealing that entities and master rating as humans. That's really critical.
segments.textZh: 因为未来真正的歧视，就是利用这些社会信用评分和人工智能系统，以各种借口把人类挡在网络之外，却任由网络机器人横行。埃隆·马斯克所做的另一件有远见的事，就是向网络机器人宣战，向那些正在窃取那些实体、并以人类身份进行主评级的机器人宣战。这确实至关重要。

segments.textEn: So one thing I did in a post today, and I think Tucker was the first one to do this and not only calling you the most censored man on the planet, he said that you were, I think the first major personality to be censored by Big Tech. And he told the story of how Tim Cook had a meeting with other platforms in 2017, end of 2017, and they made the decision to censor you not only from social media platforms, but that included your bank account.
segments.textZh: 所以我今天在一篇帖子里提到了一件事，我认为塔克是第一个这么做的人，他不仅称你为这个星球上遭受审查最严重的人，还说你是，我想，是第一个遭到大型科技公司审查的主要公众人物。他讲述了蒂姆·库克如何在2017年与其他平台开会，是在2017年底，他们决定对你实施审查，不仅把你从社交媒体平台上封禁，还包括你的银行账户。

segments.textEn: That included everything. Can you tell us more about the platforms that censored you, the excuse that they gave and the experience that you went through?
segments.textZh: 那涵盖了一切。你能否进一步告诉我们，哪些平台审查了你、它们给出了什么借口，以及你经历了什么？

segments.textEn: Absolutely. I think that was back in August of 2017, 18. I don't remember the exact date, but it was in August. And I normally get up at about 4 in the morning. So I got up, got a cup of coffee, turned the computer on, and I had hundreds of messages saying it was just announced you were banned. And Tim Cook said, yeah. We had our weekend meeting and I met with the other heads of Big Tech and we decided to curate like it's a museum and I'm a museum piece that he just took out and put something else in there.
segments.textZh: 当然。我想那是在2017年、18年的8月。我不记得确切日期了，但当时是8月。我通常凌晨4点左右起床。所以我起床后，拿了杯咖啡，打开电脑，然后收到了数百条消息，说刚刚宣布你被封禁了。蒂姆·库克说，是的。我们开了周末会议，我和其他大型科技公司的负责人见了面，我们决定像博物馆那样进行策展，而我就是一件博物馆藏品，他刚把我拿出去，又放了别的东西进去。

segments.textEn: You know, a nice word for liquidating. And then they really didn't have excuses for why they did it. They used some really, really strange excuses that I was rude to a CNN reporter, Oliver Darcy, and that I'd also beat up a child in Missouri because the guy looked like me. But it was on ABC News and it was just really, really, really flimsy reasons. And then I was taken off. We lost most of our software that we were already paying for.
segments.textZh: 你知道，这是“清除”的一种好听说法。然后，他们其实拿不出什么借口来解释为什么这么做。他们用了些非常、非常奇怪的借口，说我对CNN记者奥利弗·达西态度粗鲁，还说我在密苏里州殴打了一个孩子，因为那个人长得像我。但那是在ABC新闻上，而那些理由真的非常、非常、非常站不住脚。然后我就被下架了。我们失去了自己已经付费购买的大部分软件。

segments.textEn: We lost our shopping cart software, we lost the sub software, we lost LinkedIn. We lost over 100 things. And then we lost our banking. We launched our credit card processor. We lost over 100 things in the next week or two. And it was really, really intense. And then they had, we later learned, I'm not gonna say names or even get into it because that's what they want's attention. But we learned there was a big, powerful New York PR firm that actually does the PR for the UN and also for some of the CIA.
segments.textZh: 我们失去了购物车软件，失去了订阅软件，失去了领英。我们失去了100多样东西。然后我们失去了银行服务。我们推出了信用卡处理服务。接下来一两周里，我们失去了100多样东西。而且那真的、真的很激烈。然后他们有，我们后来得知，我不会说出名字，甚至不会深入谈，因为他们想要的就是关注。但我们了解到，有一家实力雄厚的纽约大型公关公司，实际上为联合国做公关，也为中情局的一些部门做公关。

segments.textEn: And that's really what we're talking about here. That's all come out in Congress now. And then they went and dredged up stuff in my timeline, out of context, blew it up times a million, and then said that I was currently doing things I'd never done. Just outrageous, horrible things. But notice, never proof, never a clip, never a video, never anything. And so other than like three second clips out of context, so I was unable to defend myself.
segments.textZh: 而这其实就是我们在这里谈论的事情。现在这些都已经在国会曝光了。然后他们跑去从我的时间线里挖出一些东西，断章取义，把它放大100万倍，然后说我当时正在做一些我从未做过的事。简直骇人听闻、糟糕透顶的事情。但请注意，从来没有证据，从来没有片段，从来没有视频，什么都没有。所以除了一些断章取义的3秒钟片段外，什么都没有，因此我无法为自己辩护。

segments.textEn: And so they were able to then create this new Alex Jones. But then I was very blessed. Over the next five years, the public really on their own because they kept demonizing, kept attacking some of thousands of articles a week, hundreds of TV programs a week. I'm not exaggerating. I mean, AP articles syndicated every newspaper in the country at least once a week, and daily mail attack pieces every week. Just thousands and thousands and thousands of articles like I was a third world country they were about to invade.
segments.textZh: 所以他们随后得以塑造出这个新的亚历克斯·琼斯。但之后我非常幸运。在接下来的5年里，公众真的是自发地，因为他们不断妖魔化，不断攻击，每周有数千篇文章，每周有数百个电视节目。我没有夸张。我的意思是，美联社的文章至少每周被全国每家报纸转载1次，《每日邮报》每周都有攻击性文章。就是成千上万、成千上万、成千上万篇文章，仿佛我是一个他们即将入侵的第三世界国家。

segments.textEn: There was that much propaganda, but it wasn't as they were really that scared of me. They knew in documents that later came out that once they used me as a training tool, like a chew toy for attack dogs, that once the public got scared and didn't defend me and self censored and didn't promote me, then they can move on to everybody else. So I was simply the first big domino to fall. And then once they did that, they were able to take the whole thing over.
segments.textZh: 宣传就是有那么多，但并不是因为他们真的那么害怕我。后来曝光的文件表明，他们知道，一旦他们把我当作训练工具，就像给攻击犬用的磨牙玩具，一旦公众害怕了，不为我辩护，自我审查，也不宣传我，那么他们就可以转向其他所有人。所以我只不过是第1块倒下的大型多米诺骨牌。而他们一旦这样做了，就得以接管整个局面。

segments.textEn: And since then, I mean, they had NATO summits five years ago saying we got Alex Jones and now we're going to get everybody. We're going to basically shut down, left, right, everybody. We're going to bring in total control. The Internet will soon be like Netflix. There'll only be approved channels and approved programs. These are quotes. And so I was there on still some talk radio stations, on my own website, Infowars.com, desperately trying to explain, look, they're having congressional hearings about AI censoring people.
segments.textZh: 从那以后，我是说，他们5年前在北约峰会上说，我们已经拿下亚历克斯·琼斯，现在要拿下所有人。我们基本上要让所有人闭嘴，无论左派、右派，所有人。我们要实行全面控制。互联网很快就会像 Netflix。只会有获准的频道和获准的节目。这些都是原话。所以我当时仍然在一些谈话类广播电台上，在我自己的网站 Infowars.com 上，拼命试图解释，听着，他们正在就人工智能审查人们一事举行国会听证会。

segments.textEn: They're having EU and NATO meetings. Here are the documents, here are the videos. And they were so confident then because no one was talking about it in cyberspace and was just little pockets talking about it. So they got away with it. But then they got so arrogant with the Hunter Biden laptop and with what we saw in the build up to 2020 and after that. And then they censored so many tens of millions of people, really more than that, and removed billions of posts on questioning Covid origins or questioning the Libya pull out or questioning open borders, that it just infuriated the public because they went too far.
segments.textZh: 他们在召开欧盟和北约会议。这些是文件，这些是视频。而且他们当时非常自信，因为网络空间里没人谈论这件事，只有一些小圈子在谈。所以他们蒙混过关了。但后来，在亨特·拜登笔记本电脑事件上，以及我们在2020年前夕和之后所看到的事情上，他们变得如此傲慢。然后，他们审查了数以千万计的人，实际上远不止这些，还删除了数十亿条质疑新冠病毒起源、质疑撤出利比亚或质疑开放边境的帖子，这彻底激怒了公众，因为他们做得太过火了。

segments.textEn: And then people went back and said, oh well, what happened to Alex Jones? And so they basically dug me up, did a, you know, exhumed me and did a autopsy and found out that I was just the first test subject. And so quite frankly, I'm just very honored for everybody's support and people seeing through this. I'm certainly not perfect, but 99% of what people hear about me is not true. It's the same thing they do to Elon where he says nice things and then they, they lie and say Elon Musk just said this, and then you spend an hour trying to find where he actually said what he said.
segments.textZh: 然后人们回过头来说，哦，那亚历克斯·琼斯遭遇了什么？所以他们基本上把我挖了出来，做了个，你知道，把我掘出来做了尸检，结果发现我只不过是第一个试验对象。所以坦率地说，我非常荣幸能得到大家的支持，也很荣幸人们看穿了这一切。我当然并不完美，但人们听到的关于我的事情有99%都不是真的。他们对埃隆也是这么干的，他说了一些友善的话，然后他们，他们撒谎说埃隆·马斯克刚刚说了这个，接着你要花1个小时去寻找他实际上是在哪里说了他所说的话。

segments.textEn: You finally find it and it's the opposite. And so I'm telling you folks, that's what they do. They completely twist everything. And I think so many people got a large serving of what I had that there was a lot of camaraderie. And quite frankly, everybody are veterans. I wouldn't call us victims, but we're veterans of real information war. Now we've all had a real chance to experience it. And so it's a major tide turning point.
segments.textZh: 你终于找到了，结果意思完全相反。所以各位，我告诉你们，他们就是这么干的。他们彻底歪曲一切。而我认为，太多人结结实实地尝到了我曾经遭受的待遇，因此产生了强烈的同袍情谊。坦率地说，所有人都是老兵。我不会称我们为受害者，但我们是真实信息战的老兵。现在我们都真正有机会亲身经历它了。所以这是一次重大的潮流转折点。

segments.textEn: I know that like a poison battery, they charged me up with so much negativity, such a straw man lie, such a horrible, terrible demon, that Elon knew that if he brought me back early, I think that that would have been too far because the public wasn't educated yet and he had to free the rest of the captives first. But I think as more evidence came out, he made that bold move because it's really a fuck you.
segments.textZh: 我知道，就像一块有毒的电池一样，他们用如此多的负面情绪给我充电，编造出如此荒谬的稻草人谎言，把我塑造成如此可怕、如此骇人的恶魔，以至于埃隆知道，如果他过早让我回来，我认为那会做得太过头，因为公众还没有受到教育，而他必须先释放其他被俘的人。但我认为，随着更多证据浮现，他采取了那个大胆的行动，因为这其实就是一句“去你妈的”。

segments.textEn: Just like he said a few weeks ago at the New York Times, that these people are. There's never enough censorship. You never can bend enough to them. You never can compromise with them, they never compromise with us. So you kind of. You finally reach that, well, fuck you moment. Fuck yourself moment. Go fuck yourself. And so I think that's the shot heard around the world. I think that was the final tipping point with the tide completely turned when Elon Musk said, go fuck yourself.
segments.textZh: 就像他几周前在《纽约时报》那里说的，这些人就是。审查永远不够。你对他们再怎么屈服都不够。你永远无法和他们妥协，他们从不和我们妥协。所以你有点。你最终会到达那个，好吧，去你妈的时刻。你自己滚蛋的时刻。滚你妈的。所以我认为，那是响彻世界的一枪。我认为，当埃隆·马斯克说“滚你妈的”时，那就是潮流彻底逆转的最终临界点。

segments.textEn: You can mark that day as a shot heard around the world in the infowar and when we turn the tide.
segments.textZh: 你可以把那一天标记为信息战中响彻世界的一枪，也是我们扭转潮流的那一天。

segments.textEn: So in your interview with Packer, you did express concern on what could happen, expressed understanding on why Elon didn't bring you back. Obviously that didn't last long. And you also had concerns on what could happen to Elon if he does reinstate your account now that you're back. Do you expect Elon, who also quote, I think he replied to Brian, who's on stage, one of his replies, he said, I expect revenue to potentially drop from this decision.
segments.textZh: 所以，在你接受帕克采访时，你确实表达了对可能发生之事的担忧，也表示理解埃隆为什么没有让你回来。显然，那并没有持续太久。而且你也担心，既然你现在回来了，如果埃隆恢复你的账号，他可能会遭遇什么。你是否预期埃隆——他还说过一句话，我想他是在回复台上的布赖恩，在他的一条回复中，他说，我预计这项决定可能会导致收入下降。

segments.textEn: Do you expect there to be attacks or pressure on Elon after he reinstated you?
segments.textZh: 你是否预期，埃隆在恢复你的账号后会遭到攻击或承受压力？

segments.textEn: Well, I think he said that yesterday. I don't have the comment on X in front of me, but he basically said it's the right thing to do because of principle. And it's also what the majority of the vote said. So this probably will hurt X monetarily, but justice be done, May the heavens fall, basically. But at the end of the day, it already has way more traffic, way more people. It's Avant garde. It's revolutionary, it's rebel, it's maverick.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我想他昨天说过这话。我面前没有X上的那条评论，但他基本上说，出于原则，这是正确的做法。而且这也是大多数投票者的意见。所以这可能会让X在经济上蒙受损失，但基本上就是，正义必须伸张，哪怕天塌下来。但归根结底，它已经拥有多得多的流量、多得多的人。它是前卫的。它是革命性的，是叛逆的，是特立独行的。

segments.textEn: And that's what Elon Musk has always said he is. And he's done all these maverick things. And people always say, well, he didn't really do that. But I went back and researched it. He did do that. All these incredible successes, I'm not kissing his ass. It's true. And the fact that he could take over Twitter, free it, and bring back one of the most demonized people, if not the most demonized in the world. Talk about a witch hunt.
segments.textZh: 而埃隆·马斯克一直说自己就是这样的人。而且他做了所有这些特立独行的事情。人们总是说，嗯，他并没有真的做到那些。但我回头研究过。他确实做到了。所有这些不可思议的成功，我不是在拍他马屁。这是真的。而他竟然能够接管Twitter、解放它，并让世界上最被妖魔化的人之一回来，甚至可能是最被妖魔化的那个人。真是一场猎巫。

segments.textEn: Shows he put his money where his mouth is and is the maverick's maverick. I mean, nobody can argue now that this guy is not cutting edge maverick. And so I think he understands that that's where this is going. And he's gambling on free humanity. He's betting on humanity. So when I was on Tucker, he taped it a few weeks ago because he was waiting to launch his new network to launch this Monday. But he said he waited long enough, so he went ahead and released it ahead of his new network launching Monday.
segments.textZh: 这表明他言行一致，是特立独行者中的特立独行者。我的意思是，现在没人能争辩说这家伙不是走在前沿的特立独行者了。所以我认为他明白事情正朝这个方向发展。而且他在自由的人类身上下注。他在押注人类。所以我上塔克节目时，他在几周前录了节目，因为他在等待推出自己的新网络，准备于本周一上线。但他说他已经等得够久了，所以他就在自己的新网络于周一上线之前，提前发布了节目。

segments.textEn: They'll still be here on X, but obviously some of it will be behind a paywall.
segments.textZh: 他们仍然会在X上，但显然，其中一部分内容会设在付费墙后面。

segments.textEn: I didn't think that Musk was, I mean, I knew he was a maverick, but I didn't know that he was like Top Gun. I'm just being serious. So I said, look, I understand. He knows I've been so demonized, so lied about. They built me into the devil's devil at an emotional level of so many people that, that, that, that, that they will absolutely come after him at a never before seen level. This happens. And the adl, the CIA and the Justice Department and the Southern Property Law Center, Media Matters, they were already doing it when I was taping the interview like three weeks ago.
segments.textZh: 我没想到马斯克是，我的意思是，我知道他特立独行，但我不知道他就像《壮志凌云》一样。我是认真的。所以我说，听着，我理解。他知道我被妖魔化得有多严重，人们对我撒了多少谎。他们在如此多人的情感层面上把我塑造成魔鬼中的魔鬼，以至于，那，那，那，那，那些人绝对会以前所未见的程度对付他。这种事确实会发生。而ADL、CIA、司法部、南方财产法律中心、Media Matters，在我大约3周前录制采访时，就已经在这么做了。

segments.textEn: But then since then, all those big establishment sponsors who are already being boycotted by the American people, by the way, so they're losing literally hundreds of millions of dollars in the aggregate because the people are boycotting them. As Elon said, well, now they're trying to bully Elon to bully the American people, the people of the world. So he said, go fuck yourself. And I can't speak for Elon, maybe he'll call in.
segments.textZh: 但从那以后，所有那些大型建制派赞助商——顺便说一句，他们本来就遭到美国民众抵制，所以他们总计确实损失了数亿美元，因为民众在抵制他们。正如埃隆所说，嗯，现在他们试图霸凌埃隆，以此霸凌美国人民、全世界人民。所以他说，滚你妈的。我不能代表埃隆发言，也许他会打进来。

segments.textEn: But I think as soon as they did that to him, even though he tried to basically work with them, was being very, very fair. And you know, I think really cleaned up, you know, the, the, the thing of bots and things like that, as soon as they doubled down, he said, you know what, screw you, I'll go ahead then. And release the Kraken. And it's not that I'm that good on Twitter or that I'm even that great of a talk show host.
segments.textZh: 但我认为，他们一对他这么做，尽管他曾试图基本上与他们合作，也一直非常、非常公平。而且你知道，我认为他确实清理了，你知道，机器人账号之类的，那，那，那些东西；他们一变本加厉，他就说，你知道吗，去你的，那我就干吧。放出海怪。而且这并不是因为我在Twitter上有多么出色，甚至也不是因为我是多么优秀的脱口秀主持人。

segments.textEn: It's the symbol of what they built of. Alex Jones is now an archetype of the rebel populist and what the establishment fears. And so what Elon did was really throw down the gauntlet.
segments.textZh: 这是他们塑造出的东西的象征。亚历克斯·琼斯如今已成为反叛民粹主义者以及建制派所恐惧之物的原型。所以埃隆的所作所为，实际上就是公开发起挑战。

segments.textEn: Yeah. So we've sent an invite to Elon. Hopefully he'll be able to join. He is online, so we'll see if he joins. But do you think it's enough? And I'm focusing heavily on censorship because there's a lot of things we're going to discuss here with us for a while. But I'm focusing on this because I do think it's one of the biggest threats that people are not paying attention to, to have a small amount of. To see what happened to you, to what happened to Tate as well.
segments.textZh: 是的。所以我们已经向埃隆发出了邀请。希望他能加入。他在线，所以我们看看他是否会加入。但你认为这足够吗？我现在重点谈审查，因为我们要在这里和我们一起讨论很多事情一段时间。但我专注于这点，是因为我确实认为，这是人们没有留意的最大威胁之一，拥有少量的。看看发生在你身上的事，以及同样发生在泰特身上的事。

segments.textEn: Most recently, a small group of people that can make a decision to not only deplatform someone, but essentially almost wipe them out from existence. Now, obviously, X and Rumble are making that difficult for them is a threat to democracy, something that people are not talking about and something that hasn't stopped. But do you think it's enough what Elon's doing and Rumble is doing on a much smaller scale?
segments.textZh: 最近，一个小团体可以作出决定，不仅让某个人失去平台，而且实质上几乎将其从世上抹去。现在，显然，X和Rumble正在让他们难以做到这一点，这是对民主的威胁，是人们没有谈论的事情，也是尚未停止的事情。但你认为埃隆正在做的事情，以及Rumble以小得多的规模正在做的事情，足够吗？

segments.textEn: Absolutely. I mean, what Elon Musk is doing, and I'm not trying to gush here, but it is 1776, 2.0. It is grand. It is amazing. You asked the question earlier, you know, is he in danger? I think Elon's dad is right. I mean, if you don't think Trump's in danger for what he's doing, and I'm not saying he's perfect, but he's definitely anti establishment. You're crazy if you don't think Elon is in physical danger for what he's doing.
segments.textZh: 绝对足够。我的意思是，埃隆·马斯克正在做的事情——我并不是想在这里大肆吹捧——但这就是1776，2.0。这很宏大。这令人惊叹。你之前问过那个问题，你知道，他有危险吗？我认为埃隆的父亲是对的。我的意思是，如果你不认为特朗普会因为自己的所作所为而身处险境——我不是说他完美，但他绝对反建制——那么你就是疯了，如果你不认为埃隆会因为自己的所作所为而面临人身危险的话。

segments.textEn: He is directly taking on the old rotting corporate mega bank blackrock establishment that's trying to bring in a world government, cashless society, social credit score, esgs, all of this. And he's trying to create, as he said, an alternate plan for history. But instead of forcing it down our throats, he's trying to offer people to come to the table and all of us collectively, through free market competition, add our two cents and build something that's America 2.0 or America Intergalactic a hundred point zero.
segments.textZh: 他正在直接对抗那个腐朽陈旧的企业、巨型银行、贝莱德建制派，后者正试图引入世界政府、无现金社会、社会信用评分、ESG，所有这一切。而且正如他所说，他正试图为历史创造一个替代方案。但他并没有把它硬塞进我们的喉咙，而是试图邀请人们坐到桌前，让我们所有人通过自由市场竞争共同贡献自己的微薄意见，打造出某种美国 2.0 或美国星际 100.0。

segments.textEn: And so, I mean, I've always liked Elon Musk because I would hear him talking five, six, seven years ago, and I thought that's exactly how I think on so many issues. I disagree with some things he did, but I've seen his evolution into understanding that you can't work with this establishment anymore. They're too stagnant, they're too detached from reality. They're dangerous. And it's time for a new guard. It's time for new leadership.
segments.textZh: 所以，我的意思是，我一直很喜欢埃隆·马斯克，因为我会听到他在5、6、7年前的讲话，而且我觉得，在如此多的问题上，我的想法正是如此。我不同意他做过的一些事，但我看到了他的转变，他开始明白，你再也无法与这个建制派合作了。他们太停滞不前，太脱离现实。他们很危险。现在该换一批新卫队了。现在需要新的领导层。

segments.textEn: And you see the energy of Elon Musk or the energy of Donald Trump that in of itself threatens the establishment. They have all these layers of bureaucracy and so they can deny culpability for the terrible things they're doing. And because of opening up X, it's changed the world. And we've seen the traffic explode, we've seen the engagement explode, and we've seen it accelerate the collapse of the other big tech media operations because they can only survive when there's no competition.
segments.textZh: 你可以看到埃隆·马斯克的能量，或唐纳德·特朗普的能量，这本身就在威胁建制派。他们设置了层层官僚机构，因此可以否认自己对正在做的可怕事情负有责任。而且由于开放了 X，它改变了世界。我们看到流量激增，互动量激增，而且我们看到它加速了其他大型科技媒体业务的崩溃，因为只有在没有竞争时，它们才能生存。

segments.textEn: And I know Elon doesn't want to collapse them. He wants to work with them. But they were trying to collapse the Western system of an open, free society, branding it as a neoliberal open free society, when it's really a giant totalitarian free. And so I'm just excited to be here at the dawn of 1776 part two. Now there's going to be bumps. There's going to be a lot of problems in the way Biden just said last week, and it was confirmed to also be told to Congress by the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff that if they do not give another $106 billion to Ukraine, we're going to have US troops dying soon on the ground.
segments.textZh: 而且我知道埃隆并不想让它们崩溃。他想与它们合作。但它们正试图摧毁西方开放、自由的社会体系，把它标榜为一个新自由主义的开放自由社会，而实际上它是一个巨大的极权主义自由。所以我只是很兴奋能在1776第二部的黎明时刻来到这里。现在会有坎坷。前路会有很多问题，拜登上周刚刚说过，而且也已证实参谋长联席会议主席同样对国会说过，如果他们不再向乌克兰提供1060亿美元，我们很快就会有美国军人死在地面上。

segments.textEn: Your sons, your daughters, your nephews. That's what Lloyd Austin told Congress in a closed session, but it was told directly by a congressman, word for word, that wrote it down to Tucker Carlson. And so these people are now threatening nuclear blackmail if we don't keep their money laundering operation going. It's got to end. It's got to stop now. And the world sees that and the world knows that. So I think instead of this even being a political movement, it's a worldwide renaissance 2.0 that simply doesn't want to blow the planet up and just wants common sense and wants all the crazy Hitlerian Napoleonic corporate war games to end.
segments.textZh: 你们的儿子、女儿、侄子和外甥。劳埃德·奥斯汀就是在一次闭门会议上这么告诉国会的，而一名国会议员直接把这件事逐字逐句告诉了塔克·卡尔森，那名议员还把它写了下来。所以这些人现在威胁要进行核讹诈，如果我们不让他们的洗钱行动继续下去的话。这必须结束。现在就必须停止。全世界都看到了，全世界都知道这一点。所以我认为，这甚至不再是一场政治运动，而是一场全球性的文艺复兴2.0，它只是不想炸毁这个星球，只想要常识，并希望所有疯狂的希特勒式、拿破仑式企业战争游戏都结束。

segments.textEn: And so I just think that sanity is beginning to flood back into the discourse.
segments.textZh: 所以我只是认为，理智正开始重新大量涌入公共讨论。

segments.textEn: Yeah, so we're going to talk about the Ukraine war. We're going to talk about Gaza as well. And you've talked about it on Tucker's interview. I've got a few quotes from there. It's going to take a few questions from the panel, Maybe three quick questions, Laura. And then Brian.
